DePuy Synthes
PROX TIBIA · 3.5AUS

Proximal Tibia Plates 3.5

Lateral VA-LCP™ & Medial LCP™ · Technique & Selection Guide
Lateral · VA-LCPSmall & large bend · 4–14 holes
Medial · LCP4–20 combi holes

Two plates. One 3.5 mm screw platform. Two torque limits.

Use the switch below to change between the lateral VA-LCP and the medial LCP plate — every tab follows it. Both are stainless steel, left and right, and run off Ø 3.5 mm screws with a T15 StarDrive.

Lateral VA: 2.5 Nm Medial LCP: 1.5 Nm Locking drill Ø 2.8 Cortex drill Ø 2.5 + RHH Small Frag kit

Kit check — order the RHH Small Fragment kit too

The prox tib trays do not run on their own. Both plates need the standard small fragment instrument kits from the RHH on the case to complement them — they supply the 3.5 mm cortex screws, standard 3.5 mm locking screws and the general small frag drills, guides, drivers and depth gauge. Confirm a 1.5 Nm torque limiter is on the case as well. Full checklist on the Instruments tab.

Lateral VA-LCP

anterolateral proximal tibia
VA-LCP Proximal Tibial Plate 3.5
Plate featuresVA locking holes in the head and neck take VA locking screws at ±15°. Long compression hole in the neck for the first cortex screw. VA locking Combi holes in the shaft combine compression (DCU) and VA locking. K-wire and suture holes proximally.
Small bend (SB)
Large bend (LB)
Small bend & large bendTwo contours to cover the range of tibial shapes. Choose with the SB / LB trial implants. 4–14 holes, 87–237 mm, left & right.

Article numbers: see the implant table below.
■

Associated shaft fracture: four screws per fragment are essential — choose a plate long enough to take them.

▲

Plates >12 holes: carefully dissect down to the plate before every distal trocar/sleeve to see and protect the superficial peroneal nerve and the anterior neurovascular bundle. In short patients this zone may be reached with a shorter plate.

▲

Plates are anatomically contoured — bending is not recommended. A bent plate may no longer line up with the aiming arm.

Medial LCP

anteromedial proximal tibia
Left plate shown · side and front view
Plate featuresHead: three convergent threaded holes — 3.5 locking or 3.5 conical. Two 2.0 mm holes for K-wires or meniscal sutures.
Neck: two angled locking holes that converge with the head screws.
Shaft: Combi holes (DCU + threaded) with a limited-contact profile. Slot at the end for the Articulated Tension Device.
Subchondral raftThe head screws form a raft that buttresses the medial plateau and gives fixed-angle support. 316L stainless steel only.

Planning Template

X-ray template — plan plate length and the proximal screw lengths before the case
■

Tap a step to open it. Lateral VA-LCP — 15 steps plus implant removal, condensed from the DePuy Synthes technique. Instruction by a surgeon experienced with these products is required.

1Preparation & PositioningSets · supine · fluoro
Supine, radiolucent table, knee flexed
Required sets
01.127.001VA-LCP Proximal Tibial Plates 3.5, stainless
01.127.003VA Instruments & Long Screw Insertion Instruments 3.5
01.127.004Aiming Arm Instruments for VA-LCP Proximal Tibial Plates 3.5
RackVA Locking Screws Ø 3.5 mm
RHHStandard Small Fragment instrument kit — Ø 3.5 cortex screws, drills, guides, reduction instruments

Supine on a radiolucent table, leg freely movable. Contralateral leg can go in an obstetric leg holder. AP and lateral fluoro of the proximal tibia are required.

Flex the knee over towels, or fix the thigh in a leg holder at 50°–80° flexion.

■

Lag screws may need to be planned pre-op. With an associated shaft fracture, plan four screws per fragment.

2ApproachGerdy's tubercle
Hockey stick or straight incision
Submeniscal arthrotomy

Curved (120° hockey stick) or straight incision from Gerdy's tubercle, about 50 mm distally.

About 0.5 cm from the tibial ridge, detach and retract tibialis anterior. The plate goes between periosteum and muscle — dissect the muscle attachment enough for the proximal plate to sit correctly.

For complex intra-articular fractures, an anterolateral arthrotomy under and parallel to the lateral meniscus gives control of the reduction. Secure the meniscus with resorbable stay sutures.

3Determine Plate TypeSmall bend vs large bend
Trial implant, correct side

Use the trial for the correct side to pick small bend (SB) or large bend (LB). Trials: SB R/L 03.127.012 / 013, LB R/L 03.127.014 / 015.

■

A fractured condyle may be broadened and suggest the wrong type — x-rays of the other limb help.

4Assemble Aiming ArmInsertion handle · bolt · arm
Handle pins into the 3 dimples
Confirm side R / L

Thread the nut (03.124.004) onto a cannulated interlocking bolt: 1.6 mm (03.124.005) to pass a guide wire, or 2.8 mm (03.124.006) to predrill the distal neck hole.

Lay the plate flat. Seat the insertion handle (R 03.127.007 / L 03.127.008) so its pins sit in the three dimples around the distal neck hole. Thread the bolt in until tight; tighten the nut with the 11 mm combination wrench.

Thread the connection screw into the correct side of the aiming arm (03.127.009) and secure it to the handle.

■

One aiming arm fits all four plates — check the marked side on the top and side of the arm. Short plate / proximal fracture: the arm is optional; use the head technique for shaft VA screws.

5Insert & Provisionally Fix PlateK-wires · cortex screw in long hole
Slide distally under tibialis anterior
Ø 2.0 K-wires · long hole

Slide the plate distally between tibialis anterior and periosteum, distal end kept on bone. Check position on the condyle with image intensifier or palpation.

Fix with Ø 2.0 mm K-wires (292.200.01) through the proximal or middle K-wire holes.

First screw: 3.5 cortex screw in the long hole in the plate neck. Drill Ø 2.5 mm (03.113.023) through the Universal Drill Guide 3.5 (323.360) to the medial cortex. Measure with the depth gauge 319.090. Insert with the hex 2.5 driver (314.550) on power, final tighten by hand — this buttresses the fragment to bone.

▲

Do not use the drill bit calibration for this measurement — use the depth gauge.

Tighten screw — fracture gap closes
■

To avoid the long-hole cortex screw colliding with the distal neck locking screw, check the trajectory with a long drill guide (or a 1.6 mm K-wire through the insertion handle). Plate position can still be adjusted now.

▲

Too distal = no rafting support for the joint. Too proximal = proximal screws can damage the joint.

6Reduce Articular SurfaceLag screws over the plate
Interfragmentary cortex screw

Reduction is usually done over the plate. Independent compression screws can go proximal to the plate — they must not hit the locking screws or enter the joint.

Split fracture: compress the lateral condyle with an interfragmentary 3.5 cortex screw — drill Ø 2.5 mm through 323.360 until it just penetrates the medial cortex, measure with the depth gauge, insert with the hex driver.

Confirm on fluoro: plate oriented correctly on the plateau, proximal screw paths parallel to the joint, plate aligned to the shaft in AP and lateral. Provisional wires can come out now.

■

Insert enough VA locking screws for full construct stability. Bone void filler may help support a depressed plateau.

7Secure Aiming Arm DistallyClose the “frame”
Check all connections
1.6 K-wire in most distal hole

Re-check every connection with the 11 mm wrench and 2.5 mm Allen key — firm, not excessive.

Find the aiming arm hole matching the most distal combi hole (numbered) and incise. Trocar (03.113.010) + guide sleeve (03.127.010), arrow to “LOCKING SCREW”, push down until it snaps in.

Remove the trocar, thread the centering sleeve (03.113.022) into the plate and pass a Ø 1.6 mm K-wire (02.113.001). Alternative: locking drill sleeve 2.8 (03.113.020) and drill Ø 2.8 mm (03.113.024) to the far cortex.

■

Once the frame is closed distally, the range of eccentric compression is limited. Tighten all connections before proceeding.

8Pull Reduction DeviceOptional · bring bone to plate
Through guide sleeve, locking portion

The first shaft screw can push the bone medially, especially in dense bone. The pull reduction device (03.113.015) prevents this — or use a cortex screw instead.

Use it through a guide sleeve in the locking portion of a hole (arrow to “LOCKING SCREW”). Nut at its highest, insert on power, then turn the nut down under imaging to pull bone to plate. Stop at reduction — don't over-tighten.

■

The predrilled hole takes a VA locking screw Ø 3.5 later.

9VA Screws — Proximal RowPlate head · 4 rafting screws
A · Fixed angle guide 03.127.001
B · Double guide 03.127.002, funnel

Option A — fixed angle: insert the VA fixed angle drill guide into a proximal row hole. Drill Ø 2.8 mm (324.214, 3-flute with scale) to the medial wall of the condyle. Read length off the drill bit.

Option B — variable angle (±15°): funnel end of the VA double drill guide. Drill Ø 2.8 at the angle needed to follow the plateau. Measure with depth gauge 319.090.

The four rafting screws sit parallel to the joint (and, fixed angle, to each other).

Final tightening2.5 NmHandle w/ torque limiting function 03.127.016 · by hand

Insert the VA locking screw on power with the Stardrive T15 shaft (03.113.019), then final tighten by hand with the T15 shaft on the 2.5 Nm handle. Confirm position and length before final tightening.

■

Fixed angle screws first, then variable angle screws around them. The fixed angle guide limits motion but cannot guarantee a fixed angle — watch the drill.

▲

Don't penetrate the joint (possible even at 0° with unusual plateau slope), don't collide screws, and don't place screws too close to the subchondral cartilage.

10VA Screws — Second RowPlate head
Second row — same technique

Same as step 9 — fixed angle (03.127.001) or variable angle (03.127.002 funnel end), Ø 2.8 mm drill, T15, 2.5 Nm final by hand.

■

If some head holes stay empty, spread screws across the proximal and second rows — don't just fill the proximal row.

11Cortex Screws — ShaftThrough aiming arm · before locking
Compression sleeve — correct
Wrong orientation

Incise at the chosen aiming arm hole. Trocar + guide sleeve, arrow to “CORTEX SCREW”, snap in, remove trocar.

Choose the Ø 2.5 mm drill sleeve: neutral 03.113.012 or compression 03.113.013 — open ends facing the sleeve's clamp. Drill with the Ø 2.5 mm stop drill (03.113.023).

Read the first number visible below the plastic stop

Check the plastic stop sits on the sleeve, remove the drill, read the first visible number below the stop. Or use the aiming arm depth gauge 03.113.028.

Insert on power with the hex shaft; switch to hand when the shaft marking reaches the top of the guide sleeve. Mark used holes with a stopper (03.127.011).

▲

All 3.5 cortex screws must go in before any locking screws.

12VA Screws — ShaftFixed angle or freehand ±15°
A · Locking sleeve 2.8 + stop drill
B · Spherical-head VA guide

Option A — fixed angle over the arm: guide sleeve (arrow to “LOCKING SCREW”), thread the locking drill sleeve Ø 2.8 (03.113.020) into the plate, drill with the Ø 2.8 mm stop drill (03.113.024), read the first number below the stop.

Option B — variable angle freehand: VA drill guide with spherical head (03.127.004) threaded into the protection sleeve (03.127.006), trocar (03.127.005). Press the spherical tip into the VA hole to stay within 15°. Drill Ø 2.8 with stop and read. Remove the guide, keep the protection sleeve over the hole and insert through it.

Insert with T15 on power, switch to hand near the sleeve, final tighten by hand at 2.5 Nm (03.127.016).

■

The long Ø 2.8 stop drill is calibrated for 03.127.004 and 03.113.020 only. Loosen the locking drill sleeve with the Allen key.

13Remove Aiming ArmBefore the neck holes
Remove sleeves, then arm, then bolt

Remove all guide sleeves, drill sleeves and the pull reduction device. Loosen the connecting bolt and take off the arm; then the interlocking nut, bolt and insertion handle.

Allen key 2.5 for sleeves, centering sleeves and bolt; 11 mm wrench for the arm connection and the bolt nut.

■

Alternative: predrill the distal neck hole with the long Ø 2.8 stop drill through the 2.8 mm cannulated bolt while still attached.

14VA Screws — Neck HolesDistal then proximal
Distal neck hole
Proximal neck hole

Distal neck hole: VA fixed angle guide (or double guide), drill Ø 2.8 mm (324.214) to the medial wall of the condyle, read the drill bit. T15, 2.5 Nm final by hand.

Proximal neck hole: same technique.

▲

Avoid collision — especially if the second-row or proximal-row screws were angled away from nominal.

15ClosureMeniscus · op note

Reattach the lateral meniscus to the capsule rim or to the small proximal holes in the plate. Close.

■

Record the screw recess types (Stardrive T15 / hex) in the op note to help later removal.

RImplant RemovalOptional

Only after complete consolidation, in reverse order of insertion. Through the old scar; reattach handle and aiming arm if one was used.

Unlock all screws by hand first (correct recess on handle 03.019.005), then remove them with power. Extraction set 01.900.020 for damaged screws.

▲

Plates >12 holes: dissect down to the plate to protect the superficial peroneal nerve and anterior neurovascular bundle.

■

Tap a step to open it. Medial LCP — 8 steps, condensed from the Synthes technique guide. Instruction by a surgeon experienced with these products is required.

1Preparation & PlanningSets · template · positioning
Small Fragment LCP Instrument & Implant Set
Sets
01.120.4423.5 mm LCP Medial Proximal Tibia Plate Set (plates, long locking & conical screws, 2 × Ø 2.8 drills)
105.434Required — RHH Small Fragment LCP Instrument & Implant Set. Threaded drill guides, Ø 2.5 drill, depth gauge, drivers, cortex & shaft locking screws.

Complete radiographic assessment and the pre-op plan: plate length and instruments.

▲

Important: plan the proximal screw positions and lengths so screws sit correctly in the metaphysis.

Supine on a radiolucent table. AP and lateral fluoro of the proximal tibia are required.

2Reduce Articular SurfaceCompression before locking
Large Distractor 394.35

A Large Distractor (394.35, set 115.700) or external fixator (115.720) before reduction helps visualise and reduce the joint.

Reduce and confirm on image intensifier. Independent K-wires can hold fragments; the plate's K-wire holes also help.

▲

Locking screws do not compress. Get interfragmentary compression with lag screws or 3.5 conical screws — reduce and compress the joint before applying the plate with locking screws.

■

Hold the plate to the bone to check independent lag screws won't block it.

3Position PlateMount on the plateau
2.8 threaded guide in central hole
Two Ø 2.0 K-wires

Using landmarks and fluoro, mount the plate on the intact or reconstructed plateau — don't reduce the distal fracture yet.

With the 2.8 mm threaded drill guide (312.648) on the central head hole as a handle, place a Ø 2.0 mm K-wire (292.20) through one K-wire hole. Adjust, then a second K-wire to stop rotation.

4Central Conical ScrewProvisional · pulls plate to bone
Drill Ø 2.8 parallel to joint
Read at back of the guide

Drill Ø 2.8 mm with the calibrated percutaneous drill (324.214) through the threaded guide in the central hole, under fluoro, to the lateral cortex or desired tip.

Confirm: drill parallel to the joint, reduction held, plate aligned to the shaft in AP and lateral — this sets final flexion/extension.

Length: read the drill calibration at the back of the guide, or depth gauge 319.09 through the plate.

Conical screw length−5 mm≈ 5 mm shorter than the drill reading
Torque1.5 NmTLA 511.770 / 511.773

Insert a 3.5 conical screw in the central hole with T15 (314.116) on the 1.5 Nm TLA to pull the plate to bone and compress through the plate. Or by hand with the T15 screwdriver 314.115 — gently.

▲

No TLA available? Do not tighten to the plate on power — final tighten by hand.

5Secure Plate to PlateauAnterior & posterior locking
Threaded guides, anterior & posterior holes

Threaded drill guides into the anterior and posterior head holes. Drill Ø 2.8 mm, read lengths at the back of the guides. Remove K-wires and guides.

Insert 3.5 locking screws on power with T15 on the 1.5 Nm TLA (or by hand with 314.115).

With both locked, the central conical screw can be swapped for a 3.5 locking screw.

▲

No TLA: no power for final tightening — finish by hand.

6Reduce Shaft to PlateauForceps · tension device
Bone forceps 398.81
Articulated Tension Device 321.12

Reduce the plateau to the shaft, indirectly where possible. Secure the plate to the shaft with Bone Forceps (398.81) or Plate Holding Forceps (398.811). Check rotation clinically.

If the pattern suits, load the plate in tension with the Articulated Tension Device (321.12) — compression or distraction.

■

The ATD is not in this set — it's in the Basic Instrument Set 115.04, Large Fragment LCP Set 115.400 or Periarticular LCP Set 01.240.201.

7Shaft ScrewsCortex first, then locking
Correct — cortex (1) before locking (2)
Incorrect
▲

All 3.5 cortex screws go in before any 3.5 locking screws. Once a fragment is locked, don't add a cortex screw to it without loosening and re-tightening the locking screw.

Cortex 3.5: Universal Drill Guide 3.5 (323.36) + Ø 2.5 mm drill (310.25), both cortices. Neutral: press the guide down in the DCU hole. Compression: guide at the end of the hole away from the fracture, no pressure on the spring tip. Depth gauge 319.09, insert with the small hex screwdriver (314.02).

Locking: threaded guide + Ø 2.8 drill

Locking 3.5: 2.8 threaded drill guide (312.648) into the threaded part of a Combi hole — mandatory for the screw to lock. Drill Ø 2.8 mm, read at the back of the guide (or depth gauge). T15 on the 1.5 Nm TLA.

Check the limb clinically and on x-ray — plateau correctly oriented to the shaft.

8Angled Neck HolesConverge on the head screws
Suggested lengths for convergence: 70 · 65 · 65 mm

Repeat the locking technique in the two angled holes: threaded guide, Ø 2.8 mm, T15, 1.5 Nm TLA.

With the right lengths, the angled screw tips meet the proximal head screws.

■

Securely tighten every locking screw so it locks to the plate.

▲

Lateral VA-LCP — VA locking screws torque to 2.5 Nm with the torque-limiting handle 03.127.016, final tightening by hand. A standard (non-VA) 3.5 locking screw in this plate is 0° only at 1.5 Nm.

Insertion Order

■

Cortex screws before locking screws. Long-hole cortex screw first to seat the plate → head VA screws (fixed angle first, then variable around them) → shaft cortex → shaft VA locking → neck holes after the aiming arm is off.

▲

Confirm screw position and length before final tightening at 2.5 Nm. Avoid screw collision and joint penetration — check on image intensifier.

▲

Medial LCP — locking and conical screws torque to 1.5 Nm with the Torque Limiting Attachment (511.770 / 511.773). No TLA? Never final-tighten on power — finish by hand.

■

Care

■

The 2.5 Nm handle 03.127.016 has its own IFU — recalibrate at the recommended interval. Always remove the scalpel blade before the scalpel handle goes back in the case.

Monitor for heat or pain during scanning; exclude patients with impaired thermoregulation or sensation; use low field strength and the lowest SAR possible.
